title: Why Most CEOs Are Failing Marketing’s New Math Test
gist: BCG argues CPG CEOs still run marketing on mass-media-era assumptions while insurgents like David Protein and Poppi use AI to scale with tiny teams, taking 10.8 points of breakfast-aisle share from incumbents. AI collapses content costs (a $4 product shot now costs four cents) while multiplying touchpoints and shifting discovery to LLMs, so CEOs should invest in measurement, proprietary intelligence and agent-ready processes rather than cut budgets.

themes.theme: Scale no longer guarantees CPG share

insights.claim: Small insurgent cereal and granola-bar brands gained 10.8 percentage points of market share between 2021 and 2025 while incumbent brands lost more than 12 points, showing that big marketing budgets and scale no longer guarantee growth.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Incumbent share loss to nimble challengers is measurable in the aisle; favor CPG names that are showing share gains over those defending on budget size.
insights.quote: saw their market share leap 10.8 percentage points between 2021 and 2025, while incumbent brands lost more than 12 percentage points
insights.locator: Look no further than the breakfast aisle

insights.claim: Many CPG CEOs still budget marketing through a mass-media-era lens in which size ensured share and returns were accepted on faith without hard evidence; this blind faith is now untenable.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Legacy marketing budgets at large CPG firms likely contain unmeasured waste, a potential margin lever for those who fix it and a risk for those who do not.
insights.quote: That blind faith is now untenable.
insights.locator: Old economic assumptions have a habit

insights.claim: Cutting the marketing budget because costs are rising while growth is falling is a value-destroying reflex; treating marketing as a cost to contain forfeits its potential as a growth engine.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Staples companies announcing marketing cuts to protect margins may be trading long-term share for short-term EPS.
insights.locator: The Trouble—and Opportunity—with Marketing Tribbles

themes.theme: Fragmented journeys and the content explosion

insights.claim: Consumer paths to purchase have grown from about five touchpoints a decade ago to more than 15 today, and more than half of Gen Z and Millennials research and compare options before buying.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: More touchpoints dilute each marketing dollar and push up fixed content and expertise needs, structurally pressuring marketing ROI.
insights.locator: What Tomorrow's Growth Asks of CEOs Today

insights.claim: A large-cap CPG company that once created about 500 content assets a year must now create on the order of five to six million to reach customers across channels.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A roughly 10,000x rise in required assets makes AI content production a prerequisite for coverage, not a choice.
insights.locator: The Trouble—and Opportunity—with Marketing Tribbles

insights.claim: AI is like Tribbles in Star Trek: it multiplies complexity but also makes that complexity manageable and convertible into competitive advantage.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The same technology creating marketing cost inflation supplies the tools to offset it, so net winners are those who adopt fastest.
insights.quote: AI is to marketing what Tribbles were to the Star Trek crew
insights.locator: The Trouble—and Opportunity—with Marketing Tribbles

insights.claim: Content volume is exploding while unit costs collapse: a personalized beauty product shot that cost $4 two years ago now costs four cents.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A 100x drop in asset cost shifts marketing spend away from production toward technology and measurement, hurting production agencies.
insights.quote: a highly contextualized and personalized product shot for a beauty item that cost $4 to produce two years ago now costs four cents
insights.locator: Four Dynamics Changing Marketing's Equation

insights.claim: David Protein reached $100 million in annual recurring revenue within a year of launching its first protein bar in 2024 and national distribution in two, using a 10-20 person team for content where a brand of its scale would typically deploy 50-100.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: AI-native challengers run with a fraction of incumbent headcount, compressing cost-to-scale for new entrants in staples categories.
insights.locator: David Protein's and Poppi's Lesson for CPG Goliaths

insights.claim: Poppi grew 38-fold in four years while using AI to bring marketing work in-house, with production, copywriting, research, performance optimization and measurement each needing just one full-time employee.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: In-housing via AI threatens the agency and specialist-vendor layer that incumbents rely on.
insights.locator: David Protein's and Poppi's Lesson for CPG Goliaths

insights.claim: Incumbents can be just as nimble and hold decades of accumulated intelligence, but applied poorly AI can lock them into today's technologies and erode proprietary know-how, judgment and autonomy.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Vendor lock-in and loss of tacit know-how are a hidden cost of hasty AI adoption by incumbents.
insights.locator: Incumbents, though, can be just as nimble

themes.theme: AI reshapes how consumers find and judge brands

insights.claim: In the year ending July 2026, LLM search traffic surged nearly 150%, with much of the growth in the last five months of the period.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Accelerating LLM search adoption means brand discovery is migrating quickly from traditional search and social.
insights.quote: In the year ending July 2026, LLM search traffic surged nearly 150%
insights.locator: What Tomorrow's Growth Asks of CEOs Today

insights.claim: A BCG survey of 13,000 consumers in 12 markets found nearly a third use AI in the purchase journey (a threefold increase in 18 months), about 20% routinely, and 13% ultimately buy products the AI recommends.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Agentic shopping is already converting at a measurable rate, making LLM visibility a real revenue channel.
insights.locator: AI is changing both sides of the growth equation

insights.claim: Answer engine optimization and generative engine optimization increasingly determine which CPG brands gain visibility.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Expect budget to shift from classic SEO and media toward AEO/GEO specialists and structured product data.
insights.locator: What Tomorrow's Growth Asks of CEOs Today

insights.claim: LLMs do not just shortlist products; they evaluate them using web content including unflattering reviews and conversations brands do not control, which can unravel a campaign message if the product underperforms its promises.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Product quality and promise-performance gaps become more punishing to brands, favoring genuinely good products over advertised ones.
insights.locator: This has profound implications for how

insights.claim: Leading marketing functions are structuring product data so AI systems can surface it, and laying groundwork for agentic commerce, where an AI agent handles the journey from discovery through purchase on a user's behalf.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Agentic commerce could shift brand power to whoever controls the agent interface and product-data feeds.
insights.locator: 5. Are we investing in the customer journey

themes.theme: Reorganizing marketing work across humans, agents and agencies

insights.claim: Roughly a third of CMOs in a BCG survey already pair AI agents with human oversight and redesign workflows so one human strategist orchestrates campaigns end-to-end while agents execute across creation, activation and optimization, replacing siloed channel specialists.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Channel-specialist roles and the agencies built around them are exposed to consolidation.
insights.locator: Humans, agents, and agencies are dividing marketing work differently

insights.claim: In BCG's survey of 300 CMOs, nearly all said AI is driving end-to-end transformation of their function, but more than two-thirds had yet to move beyond the basics.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Most of the adoption curve is still ahead, leaving room for laggards to fall behind and vendors to sell into.
insights.locator: Marketing departments do see this change happening

insights.claim: Agencies are moving from compensation based on a percentage of ad spend toward value-based models that share AI-enabled productivity gains with clients, while remaining needed for elite creative and specialized work such as influencer selection and LLM optimization.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Percent-of-spend agency economics are threatened; holding-company revenue models face pressure.
insights.locator: Marketing's redesign extends to agencies as well

insights.claim: As AI drives content costs down, budgets shift toward applications, cloud computing and token spend, so marketing dollars generate different returns across line items.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Marketing budgets become a demand source for cloud and model vendors while production spend shrinks.
insights.locator: Marketing dollars are generating different returns

insights.claim: Agentic AI can improve ROI of media and customer activation threefold by accelerating campaign speed and quality while lowering costs.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Claimed uplift is illustrative and unsourced, so treat as a vendor-style upper bound.
insights.locator: Marketing dollars are generating different returns

themes.theme: Measurement and proprietary intelligence as the moat

insights.claim: Leading agentic marketing organizations prioritize measurement and an intelligence layer first, codifying KPIs, brand guardrails and operating rules; one entertainment company cut time to launch and measure a campaign by 90% and tripled ROI.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Measurement infrastructure, not model access, is the early differentiator in AI marketing.
insights.locator: The Agentic Advantage Starts with Measurement

insights.claim: A global CPG company's insights agent for campaign briefs was only 50% accurate until it codified how top marketers build briefs and apply quality checks; accuracy then rose above 90% and saved more than 3,000 marketers weeks of effort annually.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Codified tacit expertise, not raw data, turns generic AI into proprietary advantage.
insights.locator: 4. How are we building unique competitive advantage

insights.claim: Companies must keep control of unique intelligence such as brand guardrails and tacit expertise, yet make it available to agents without tying it to one model, platform or vendor.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Model-agnostic portability of proprietary context is a key requirement and a point of vendor leverage.
insights.locator: As agents take on more

insights.claim: Upper-funnel brand spend should be measured against leading indicators like consideration and mindshare, while mid- and lower-funnel spend can be measured against sales and conversion; marketing ROI will become more knowable but never perfectly knowable.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Not all marketing should be forced into one ROI metric; brand spending needs separate leading-indicator scorecards.
insights.locator: Upper-Funnel Brand Investment Can and Should Be Measured

insights.claim: BCG recommends a brand-health scorecard spanning awareness, consideration, trial and conversion, sales and marketing share, and marketing ROI, embedded within six months with real-time alerts and kept in-house rather than outsourced.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Measurement is treated as a core in-house capability, implying less outsourcing to agencies.
insights.locator: For companies that have not already established

insights.claim: BCG frames CEO oversight of marketing transformation through five questions: spend less or grow more with AI; trusted measurement; end-to-end process redesign; non-replicable agentic advantage; investing in the emerging versus known customer journey.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Gives a checklist for assessing CPG management's AI-marketing credibility on earnings calls.
insights.locator: What Tomorrow's Growth Asks of CEOs Today

insights.claim: CEOs should weigh CMO requests for AI investment against AI-driven gains across the whole organization rather than as a standalone increase in marketing spend, and shift talent mix toward more scientists.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: AI marketing spend may be reclassified as enterprise productivity investment, altering how cost ratios are read.
insights.locator: 3. How are we reshaping major end-to-end processes
